title: AI is changing work faster than the data can keep up

content_html:
Sebastian Herrera

Sat, August 8, 2026 at 7:00 AM CDT 8 min read

No one can agree on whether AI is taking away jobs.

Recent studies have shown AI having a positive impact on job growth and opportunities, yet large groups of economists, as well as labor activists, warn that the emerging technology threatens to quickly transform the financial system, and that action must be taken now.

Tech companies, especially large ones, have continued to cull jobs during the AI boom. Microsoft laid off nearly 5,000 people in early July as it continues to pour billions into AI data centers. The layoffs added to earlier downsizing by the software giant and moves by companies that include Amazon and Oracle to shed thousands of people in the last two years.

But whether AI is directly leading to job cuts has been difficult to measure, and the picture is blurred by corporate whiplash: CEOs blame AI for layoffs one month, then hail it as an engine for new job creation the next. Even recently, some of the largest companies, such as Google parent Alphabet, have reportedly told investors they plan to increase headcount.

"There's been discretion out there as to what extent the layoffs we have been observing are really driven by AI," Till Von Wachter, a professor of economics at the University of California, Los Angeles, told Fortune. "It's been notoriously hard to pin that down."

Some economists, such as Ben Zipperer from the Economic Policy Institute, said AI's impact on jobs has so far been more limited than what some doomsday scenarios initially predicted. 

The latest U.S. jobs report, which revealed that employers unexpectedly cut 23,000 jobs in July, only added to the confusion.

And some recent data has shown a bullish picture. A recent study by financial services firm Ramp of more than 21,000 U.S. firms found that companies that invested in AI grew their headcount. Ramp categorized its heaviest AI spenders as "high-intensity" adopters. Over two years, these top spenders expanded their overall staff by 10% and boosted entry-level hiring by 12%, defying other reports that college graduates face a barren job market. By contrast, the bottom two-thirds of adopters saw no headcount growth at all.

Though the study found general AI adopters tended to be larger firms, the most intense adopters were smaller companies which might already be growing regardless of AI and are more open to experimentation. High-intensity companies were utilizing more advanced tools like coding agents or APIs (protocols that allow various applications to communicate).

The Ramp study has parallels to a recent report by researchers at Google that found AI so far is mostly being used as a collaborative tool rather than an outright job-replacer.

content_html_zh:
塞巴斯蒂安·埃雷拉

2026 年 8 月 8 日星期六上午 7:00 CDT 阅读 8 分钟

没有人能够就人工智能是否正在夺走工作岗位达成一致。

最近的研究表明人工智能对就业增长和机会产生积极影响，但大量经济学家和劳工活动家警告说，新兴技术可能会迅速改变金融体系，必须立即采取行动。

在人工智能热潮期间，科技公司，尤其是大型科技公司，不断裁员。 微软在 7 月初解雇了近 5000 名员工，同时继续向人工智能数据中心投入数十亿美元。 此次裁员进一步加剧了这家软件巨头此前的裁员计划，以及亚马逊和甲骨文等公司在过去两年中裁员数千人的举措。

但人工智能是否会直接导致裁员一直很难衡量，而且企业的鞭打也使情况变得模糊：首席执行官们在一个月内将裁员归咎于人工智能，然后在下个月将其誉为创造新就业机会的引擎。 据报道，即使在最近，谷歌母公司 Alphabet 等一些最大的公司也已告诉投资者，他们计划增加员工人数。

加州大学洛杉矶分校经济学教授蒂尔·冯·瓦赫特 (Till Von Wachter) 向《财富》杂志表示：“对于我们观察到的裁员在多大程度上真正是由人工智能驱动的，人们有一定的判断力。” “众所周知，很难确定这一点。”

经济政策研究所的本·齐珀勒等一些经济学家表示，迄今为止，人工智能对就业的影响比一些世界末日场景最初预测的要有限。

最新的美国就业报告显示，雇主在 7 月份意外裁员 23,000 人，这进一步加剧了混乱。

最近的一些数据显示出乐观的前景。 金融服务公司 Ramp 最近对 21,000 多家美国公司进行的一项研究发现，投资人工智能的公司增加了员工人数。 Ramp 将人工智能支出最多的用户归类为“高强度”采用者。 两年多来，这些支出最高的企业将员工总数扩大了 10%，初级招聘人数增加了 12%，与其他关于大学毕业生面临就业市场贫瘠的报道相悖。 相比之下，底部三分之二的采用者人数根本没有增长。

尽管研究发现，人工智能的一般采用者往往是较大的公司，但最积极的采用者是较小的公司，无论人工智能如何，这些公司可能已经在增长，并且对实验更加开放。 高强度公司正在使用更先进的工具，例如编码代理或 API（允许各种应用程序进行通信的协议）。

Ramp 的研究与谷歌研究人员最近的一份报告相似，该报告发现人工智能迄今为止主要被用作协作工具，而不是彻底的工作替代者。
